narrative_profile: International thriller-romance, mystery, suspense, action, amnesia, and dark romance told in dual third-person limited POV. The main action unfolds continuously over roughly five hours, from shortly after midnight until sunrise, followed by an epilogue months later.
surface_case: An amnesiac woman spends one night trying to prove she did not order her own sister's murder, while the assassin she apparently hired counts down to a deadline he refuses to explain. She thinks she is investigating a crime. She thinks the man beside her is either her executioner or her only witness. She thinks if she can recover her memory before sunrise, she will be free.
true_case: Her handler spent two years feeding her falsified targets so that her assassin would eliminate seven witnesses to his private weapons network. When she found out, she did not run — she built a trap that required her own destruction. She staged her sister's death as bait, hid the complete transaction ledger inside her own conditioned reflexes, erased her memory so no interrogation could reach it, and ordered her lover to kill her if the handler ever restored the obedient version of her he had trained. But the handler had planned for her discovery too. Her rebellion was a step in his design. What he did not plan for is that she wrote over his ending. The night is not her recovering the truth. It is her executing a plan she can no longer remember making, using a body that remembers everything.
core_question: Who shot Mara Mercer on the rooftop, and why does the contract in Sloane's own handwriting order her own death at sunrise? What happened during the three months she cannot remember?
emotional_question: Can Sloane trust the man who was her lover and is now her executioner? Can she accept that she willingly became part of the system she despises? Can love survive when one partner can't remember ever falling in love?
book1_promise: One night of relentless tension as a woman with erased memory hunts for the truth behind her own death contract, while the assassin who loves her counts down to sunrise.
series_door_opened: The weapons network Rook served extends beyond his death — the ledger names enforcers and buyers who remain active, and the binding condition on Lucian's contract is proven to outlast Rook, threatening their fragile future.
book2_hook: The network Rook fed did not die with him. The ledger named everyone — including the people who paid. Someone in those pages has Lucian's contract file, and the condition that binds him did not end when Rook did.
reader_payoff_book1: The complete truth behind the three-month gap, the staged shooting, and the death contract; a hard-won romantic confirmation; a satisfying takedown of the handler; and a glimpse of a future that exists against the odds.
